summary.text: Brittany LeClear-Ping is the Republican candidate for the New Hampshire House of Representatives, Hillsborough 22, in the November 3, 2026 general election, after advancing from the September 8 Republican primary.
LeClear-Ping has a human resources background and has run for the Manchester school board, the state House and the state Senate in earlier years.

paragraphs.text: Brittany LeClear-Ping earned an undergraduate degree at Ball State University and an M.B.A. at Southern New Hampshire University, according to Ballotpedia.
LeClear-Ping worked as a human resources generalist from 2012 to 2017 and has been an office manager and realtor since 2017.
LeClear-Ping ran for the Manchester Board of School Committee, Ward 11, in 2021 and lost to incumbent Nicole Leapley, and ran at-large for the same board in 2023.
In 2022 LeClear-Ping and Carla Gericke advanced from the Republican primary for Hillsborough 22 but lost the general election to incumbents Patricia Cornell and Nicole Leapley.
In 2024 LeClear-Ping was the Republican nominee for New Hampshire State Senate District 20 and lost to Patrick Long.
Ballotpedia also lists LeClear-Ping as a withdrawn candidate in the 2026 State Senate District 20 race.

In a 2019 Ballotpedia survey for the school committee race, LeClear-Ping described herself as a parent of two small children and said education and professional experience were rooted in human resources management.
